questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Serbia?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Serbia article.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Serbia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Culture” part of the Serbia article.

questions.proof: The official language, Serbian, is written in both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “To the west of Serbia are the countries _____ (the country that was once united with Serbia), Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “countries”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Serbia article.

questions.proof: To the west of Serbia are the countries Montenegro (the country that was once united with Serbia), Bosnia and Herzegovina and Croatia.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “To the south of Serbia is the country North Macedonia and _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Macedonia”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Serbia article.

questions.proof: To the south of Serbia is the country North Macedonia and Kosovo.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “To the north of Serbia is the country _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “country”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Serbia article.
